text:
mira: FYI we just got a customer escalation — p95 jumped ~2x after canary of runtime v4.2.1 rolled to 15% traffic. seeing a mix of latency and some 429 auth failures. filing here to triage :eyes:

kai: saw the alert too. which group? any trace ids from the errors?

mira: Account: payflow-inc, impacted routes: /v1/generate and /v1/chat. example trace id from logs: trace-3f9a7b. attaching one sample log line below.

mira: ```
2026-03-17T14:03:12Z service=runtime request_id=trace-3f9a7b route=/v1/generate latency_ms=780 p95_prev=210 p95_now=460 auth_status=429
```

alex: that latency jump aligns with the kernel selector change in v4.2.1 (LUT path reordering). we changed batch-sizing heuristics and added new fallback for small-batch hotpath. could be causing cold-cache overhead.

ryan: also seeing auth 429s in the same time window. billing-bot shows a surge in token requests for payflow-inc around 14:01-14:05, might be retry storms.

billing-bot: payflow-inc spike: +3.1x requests vs baseline, many small requests (avg tokens 12). flagged possible client-side retry loop.

sam: can we correlate by host? maybe a set of pods got the new runtime and hit upstream auth at higher QPS causing 429s.

mira: good idea. kai, can you run a per-pod traffic split for the canary range? `kubectl get pods -l app=runtime -o wide` then map revision v4.2.1 pods.

kai: running quick map now, returning pods: runtime-421-a (v4.2.1), runtime-421-b (v4.2.1), runtime-410-x (v4.1.0).

kai: traffic by pod: runtime-421-a 8k rps, runtime-421-b 7.5k rps, older pods combined 80k rps. percent looks normal for 10-15% canary.

alex: can you pull p95/p99 per-pod for the window 14:00-14:10? `promql: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(runtime_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,pod))`

kai: p95 results: runtime-421-a=480ms, runtime-421-b=470ms, runtime-410-x=220ms. p99: 421-a=920ms, 421-b=880ms, 410-x=350ms.

mira: OK that pins it to the new runtime pods. next: is it the kernel selection change or the batching heuristic? alex, which PRs were in the v4.2.1 bundle?

alex: v4.2.1 includes: PR#1423 kernel-selector LUT reorder, PR#1431 adaptive-batcher improvement, PR#1440 auth-client backoff tweak (opt-in).

ryan: auth-client backoff tweak could affect 429 handling; but seeing 429s client-side suggests upstream auth service is rate-limiting. check headers from auth. any `Retry-After` returned?

mira: log snippet shows `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="auth", error=\"insufficient_scope\"` and 429 with no Retry-After in many samples. suspect client retries without exponential backoff -> amplification.

sam: repro plan: 1) route 100% test traffic to a single v4.2.1 pod in staging with synthetic small-request churn, 2) enable debug auth headers, 3) capture upstream auth responses + client retry timings.

kai: I can run the repro in staging. spinning up load job NOW: `k6 run --vus 200 --duration 5m script-small-reqs.js --env route=/v1/generate`

deploy-bot: Canary deploy event: runtime v4.2.1 promoted to 15% at 2026-03-17T13:59:40Z by @alex :shipit:

ops-bot: Incident annotated: INC-2026-0317-01 created (p95 regression, auth 429 correlation).

kai: repro results in staging: p95 ~460ms, auth 429 spikes at 14:11:22 (matching pattern). captured headers show 429 without Retry-After ~60% of the time.

alex: That suggests upstream auth doesn't set Retry-After reliably, and our auth-client change removed jitter/backoff in the fastpath. revert idea: roll back PR#1440 first (auth-client backoff tweak) and see if 429s drop.

mira: agree — PR#1440 is lower risk than kernel selector. rollout plan: rollback PR#1440 config in canary only (hotfix) and observe for 10m. if p95 drops and 429s disappear, we keep kernel change and rework backoff.

sam: can we implement ephemeral client-side circuit-breaker in front of auth to short-circuit retries while we patch? e.g., reject repeat auth attempts for 2s per token.

ryan: quick mitigation: apply a rate-limiter patch to runtime pods: set `AUTH_CLIENT_MAX_RETRIES=2` and `AUTH_CLIENT_BASE_DELAY_MS=150` via configmap and rollout to canary only.

kai: applied to runtime-421-a and runtime-421-b. configmap rollout done at 14:18:00.

mira: monitoring...

kai: after patch: p95 on canary pods dropped to 230ms within 3 minutes. auth 429s decreased by ~85%. overall platform p95 back to normal.

mira: excellent. next steps: 1) open a rollback PR for PR#1440 to revert change, 2) implement improved backoff with jitter and honor upstream Retry-After, 3) add better tracing to auth client for future triage, 4) add canary gating metric for auth 5xx/429 rate before promotion.

alex: I'll file PRs and link them here. PR-rollback: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1502 (revert auth tweak).

ryan: also suggest we add an automated bisect run in CI that runs a small synthetic load against canary to fail promotion if p95 increases >25% vs baseline in 5m window.

mira: agreed. create ticket in backlog and add as must-have for next release.

ops-bot: Postmortem checklist created and assigned to mira, alex, kai.

mira: summary for support: told customer we detected canary-induced auth retry amplification, applied config limiter, reverted change, monitoring shows normalized latency, will follow up with permanent fix and PR.

payflow-support (private msg): customer replied "Thanks Mira — seeing normal perf again, will report if anything else." :thumbsup:

mira: closing thread unless new signals. leaving incident open for postmortem and action items.

kai: saving logs + traces: S3 path s3://redwood-ops/incident/3678901234/

alex: noted lessons: be conservative with client-side retry changes, canary gating must include auth error-rate threshold, good job team. :clap:

mira: thanks all.
